answer: One stitched sail panel buys a seat: a newcomer hand-sews one panel from a marked thread, and two sailmakers hold a mirror behind it to catch light through loose seams before the gale test. A panel whose seams split, or whose thread strays from the mark, is cut down and burned with its forty hours of work. Each panel costs forty hours and $180 of sailcloth, so a hundred fakes would demand four thousand hours and $18,000 of cloth in ash.
